Yes, the fiber product $(X\setminus W)\times_X Y$ is canonically isomorphic to $Y\setminus(W\times_X Y)$, and $l$ is the base change of $k$ along $f$.

**Proof.**

Let $\mathcal I\subset\mathcal O_X$ be the quasi-coherent ideal sheaf defining the closed immersion $j:W\hookrightarrow X$, so that $|W|=V(\mathcal I)\subset|X|$. The base-changed closed immersion $j':W\times_X Y\hookrightarrow Y$ is the closed subscheme of $Y$ defined by the inverse-image ideal sheaf
$$\mathcal J:=f^{-1}\mathcal I\cdot\mathcal O_Y\subset\mathcal O_Y,$$
so $|W\times_X Y|=V(\mathcal J)\subset|Y|$.

**Claim.** $V(\mathcal J)=f^{-1}(V(\mathcal I))$ as subsets of $|Y|$.

*Proof of claim.* For $y\in Y$ with $x=f(y)$, the stalk is $\mathcal J_y=f^\#_y(\mathcal I_x)\cdot\mathcal O_{Y,y}$. Now $y\in V(\mathcal J)$ iff the image of $\mathcal J_y$ in $\kappa(y)$ is zero, iff the image of $\mathcal I_x$ in $\kappa(y)$ (via $\mathcal O_{X,x}\to\kappa(x)\to\kappa(y)$) is zero. Since $\kappa(x)\to\kappa(y)$ is a field extension, hence injective, this image is zero iff the image of $\mathcal I_x$ in $\kappa(x)$ is zero, iff $x\in V(\mathcal I)$. Thus $y\in V(\mathcal J)\iff f(y)\in V(\mathcal I)$, i.e. $V(\mathcal J)=f^{-1}(V(\mathcal I))$. $\square$

Consequently the underlying open subset of $Y\setminus(W\times_X Y)$ is
$$|Y|\setminus V(\mathcal J)=|Y|\setminus f^{-1}(V(\mathcal I))=f^{-1}\bigl(|X|\setminus V(\mathcal I)\bigr)=f^{-1}(|X\setminus W|).$$

On the other hand, $k:X\setminus W\hookrightarrow X$ is an open immersion, and the base change of an open immersion along $f$ is canonically the preimage open subscheme: $(X\setminus W)\times_X Y\cong f^{-1}(X\setminus W)$ as an open subscheme of $Y$, with underlying open subset $f^{-1}(|X\setminus W|)$.

Thus both $l:Y\setminus(W\times_X Y)\to Y$ and the base change $k':(X\setminus W)\times_X Y\to Y$ are open immersions into $Y$ supported on the *same* open subset $f^{-1}(|X\setminus W|)\subset|Y|$. An open subscheme of $Y$ is uniquely determined by its underlying open subset (the structure sheaf being $\mathcal O_Y$ restricted to that open set), and an open immersion into $Y$ with a given image is uniquely an isomorphism onto the corresponding open subscheme. Hence there is a unique $Y$-isomorphism
$$Y\setminus(W\times_X Y)\;\xrightarrow{\;\sim\;}\;(X\setminus W)\times_X Y,$$
i.e. $l$ is (up to unique isomorphism) the base change of $k$ along $f$. $\square$
